functional_requirements.title: observeOutcome core join + classification, with a durable dispatch-key fix in publisher/index.js
functional_requirements.description: New lib/marketing/observer/observe-outcome.js exports observeOutcome({supabase, correlationId, mode}). It reads the venture_channel_publish_ledger row by correlation_id, then joins campaign_content on campaign_content.idempotency_key = ledger.correlation_id (both are the identical `${ventureId}:${content.id}:${platform}:<ts>` string built once in lib/marketing/publisher/index.js:39 and reused for both writes -- confirmed by direct read, no new correlation scheme). This recovers campaign_content.external_post_id and platform, which the ledger itself never stores. If the join yields no campaign_content row, or external_post_id is null (publish failed before a post existed), classify 'unmeasurable' rather than 'unknown' -- the artifact needed to ever measure this row does not exist and never will. Additionally, a literal `dry-run-*` sentinel value in campaign_content.external_post_id (emitted by both adapters in dry-run mode) must be rejected the same as a null external_post_id -- classify unmeasurable, never treat the sentinel as a real post id. campaign_content row existence alone does not prove a successful publish: the write is guarded by `if (result.success && campaignId)` in publisher/index.js, but campaign_content is ALSO written ungated by content-generator.js, so external_post_id must be checked non-null and non-sentinel, not row presence. CRITICAL FIX REQUIRED IN lib/marketing/publisher/index.js (confirmed root cause, not a workaround): publish() currently rebuilds a fresh timestamp-keyed idempotencyKey on every call and uses that SAME local variable both as the correlationId passed INTO checkPublishAuthorization and as the key for campaign_content's own dedup-check/upsert. checkPublishAuthorization's 'already accepted' branch (autonomy-gate.js:398-405) looks up the ledger row by (venture_id, channel_type, content_ref) and returns the STORED historical correlation_id from whenever that row was originally proposed/accepted -- which differs from the freshly-built key on any attempt after the first. THE FIX: after authCheck resolves with allowed:true, publisher/index.js must use `authCheck.correlationId` (never its own locally-rebuilt idempotencyKey) as the key for both the campaign_content dedup SELECT (:69-70) and the final upsert (:179-180). This makes campaign_content.idempotency_key durably equal to venture_channel_publish_ledger.correlation_id for a given decision regardless of how many propose/deny/approve attempts preceded the real dispatch -- the actual fix the observer's join depends on. The locally-built idempotencyKey remains the value SEEDED into checkPublishAuthorization's correlationId parameter for a brand-new (never-before-seen) propose, which is unaffected.
acceptance_criteria: observeOutcome({correlationId}) for a ledger row with a matching campaign_content row returns the platform and external_post_id recovered via the idempotency_key join
observeOutcome for a ledger row with no matching campaign_content row (or a null external_post_id) returns outcome='unmeasurable', never 'unknown' and never a guess
A campaign_content row whose external_post_id is null or a literal dry-run-* sentinel classifies unmeasurable, never shipped_clean/reverted/caused_rework
publisher/index.js's campaign_content dedup-check and final upsert both key on authCheck.correlationId, never on the function-local freshly-built idempotencyKey, once authCheck has resolved

A real two-attempt approval-gated publish sequence (attempt 1 denied/pending, chairman approves, attempt 2 succeeds) yields a NON-NULL external_post_id when joined via observeOutcome -- proven by an integration test driving the actual publish()/checkPublishAuthorization() sequence, never a hand-seeded fixture that encodes the premise instead of testing it

functional_requirements.title: Scheduled observer step (never called from publish())
functional_requirements.description: New scripts/cron/publish-outcome-observer.mjs following this repo's established scheduled-job convention: parseArgs/main(argv,deps)/--once/--dry-run/Windows-safe gracefulExit, a matching .github/workflows/publish-outcome-observer-cron.yml (schedule: + workflow_dispatch), lib/machinery-class/armed-registration.js registerArmedMachinery, and lib/periodic-liveness/stamp-last-fired.js -- NOT the lib/eva/workers/ BaseWorker/WorkerScheduler setInterval pattern (wrong shape, does not survive process restarts). It selects ledger rows still outcome='unknown' whose created_at is inside a fixed observation window, calls observeOutcome per row, then calls recordPublishOutcome({correlationId, outcome, outcomeRef}) -- the ledger's own existing rule (autonomy-gate.js comment at :440-ish / confirmed by direct read) that recordPublishOutcome is never called from publish() itself. This scheduled step SUPERSEDES the still-owed inline recordPublishOutcome() call from the dependency SD (SD-LEO-INFRA-DEMAND-ENGINE-FAIL-001 shipped FR-3 known-incomplete: content-pipeline.js / owned-audience-content-loop.js still owe an inline call). That inline call must NOT be built -- it is the self-report anti-pattern the ledger docstring itself forbids, and building both would create two conflicting writers of the same row. VISIBILITY (Blocker 4): live measurement at PLAN time found venture_channel_publish_ledger has 3 rows, ALL decision='pending'/outcome='unknown', and campaign_content has 0 rows -- the observer's real-world join has nothing to act on yet. The scheduled step's main() must return/report rows_selected, rows_joined, and rows_unmeasurable counts in its summary object (repo convention: main(argv, deps) returns {exitCode, action, summary}) so a 0/0 run reads as 'ran, nothing to do' rather than silently looking wired when it is not.
acceptance_criteria: Running the script twice against the same window is idempotent: the second run changes zero rows (keyed on correlation_id, matching the ledger's own UNIQUE(correlation_id) constraint)
The script never runs from inside publisher/index.js publish() -- verified by grep showing no import of the observer module in that file
main()'s returned summary includes rows_selected/rows_joined/rows_unmeasurable counters, asserted directly by the wiring test

functional_requirements.title: Mode-aware outcome recording -- net-new, not a reuse of an existing pattern
functional_requirements.description: VALIDATION (LEAD phase, sub-agent evidence 8057d0a8) measured that execution_mode is ALREADY APPLIED in the live schema (with mock_run_id; all 3 current ledger rows are execution_mode='live') -- the prior premise that this column was 'chairman-gated, not yet applied' is FALSE, and evaluateGraduation's existing 42703-fallback branch is now dead code (left in place, not removed by this SD -- out of scope to touch). The REAL gap validation found: recordPublishOutcome (lib/marketing/autonomy-gate.js:469) does a bare `.eq('correlation_id')` update with NO execution_mode filter at all -- a mock-mode outcome as written today WOULD silently overwrite a live row's outcome. This SD must ADD an execution_mode-scoped predicate to that update (match the row's own recorded execution_mode, never cross-write). evaluateGraduation (:497) is only partially mode-aware: it currently BREAKS the streak when it encounters a mock-mode row rather than filtering candidate rows by mode up front -- this SD replaces that behavior with an explicit mode filter on evaluateGraduation's SELECT (:509), so a mock-mode call only ever considers mock-mode rows and a live-mode call only ever considers live-mode rows. This is a design decision made explicitly here, not left ambiguous.
acceptance_criteria: recordPublishOutcome's UPDATE includes an execution_mode predicate matching the row being recorded (net-new code this SD -- today's implementation has none)
evaluateGraduation's candidate-row SELECT filters by execution_mode up front; it no longer relies on breaking the streak when a mismatched-mode row is encountered
A mock-mode outcome recorded via the scheduled step never changes a live-mode row's outcome or clean_streak, verified directly (TS-3, TS-6)

functional_requirements.title: Widen the outcome domain safely: SQL CHECK, JS allowlist, AND the graduation streak-window query
functional_requirements.description: database/migrations/<date>_venture_channel_publish_ledger_outcome_unmeasurable.sql widens venture_channel_publish_ledger's outcome CHECK constraint from ('unknown','shipped_clean','reverted','caused_rework') to add 'unmeasurable', mirroring the sibling solomon_advice_outcome_ledger precedent (database/migrations/20260828_solomon_ledger_outcome_unmeasurable.sql) exactly: purely additive DROP+re-ADD of the same named constraint, no column added, no data rewritten. No 'rework' detector is invented -- direct reads of lib/marketing/ai/metrics-ingestor.js and lib/marketing/ai/variant-outcome-derivation.js confirmed neither reads or derives per-post rework/outcome state today (metrics-ingestor normalizes inbound aggregate engagement metrics; variant-outcome-derivation derives A/B success/failure from daily_rollups impression/conversion aggregates), so caused_rework is only ever set from an explicit, already-existing rework signal if one is later wired elsewhere -- this SD does not fabricate one. This SD does not remove or alter the existing 'caused_rework' CHECK value -- it remains a valid enum member -- but no code path in this SD produces it: caused_rework is explicitly declared UNREACHABLE this increment (no rework signal exists anywhere in the codebase, confirmed independently by both LEAD's direct read and VALIDATION's re-check of metrics-ingestor.js and variant-outcome-derivation.js). A future SD wires an actual rework signal before caused_rework is ever written by this pipeline. TWO ADDITIONAL FIXES REQUIRED, found by TESTING PLAN review (evidence 26462519), without which FR-6's own acceptance criterion passes green while the feature is broken: (1) recordPublishOutcome (autonomy-gate.js:470) hard-validates `['shipped_clean','reverted','caused_rework']` and THROWS on anything else -- widening only the SQL CHECK constraint means the FIRST call with outcome='unmeasurable' throws in JS before ever reaching the database. The JS allowlist must be widened to include 'unmeasurable' in the SAME change. (2) evaluateGraduation's streak-window query (autonomy-gate.js:509,523) uses `.neq('outcome','unknown')` to select candidate rows -- today 'unmeasurable' rows would newly ENTER that window (since they are not literally 'unknown'), where the loop's `else break` treats any non-shipped_clean row as a streak-breaker, silently demoting/resetting channels the moment an unmeasurable row appears. The query must exclude BOTH 'unknown' AND 'unmeasurable' from the streak window (e.g. `.not('outcome', 'in', '(unknown,unmeasurable)')`), so an unmeasurable row is invisible to the graduation safety valve exactly like an unknown row is today -- neither a clean win nor a streak-breaker.
acceptance_criteria: The outcome CHECK constraint on venture_channel_publish_ledger accepts 'unmeasurable' after migration apply
No new heuristic 'rework' classifier is added by this SD; caused_rework is only ever produced by an existing, already-verified signal (none exists today, so it is not exercised by the new code path)
recordPublishOutcome accepts 'unmeasurable' without throwing (unit test, no live DB required)
Seeding an 'unmeasurable' row leaves clean_streak/autonomy_state identical to leaving that same row 'unknown' -- a direct regression test, since this is the graduation safety valve

functional_requirements.title: Fixed observation window, never guess on an unreadable post
functional_requirements.description: The observation window (config constant, default matching the SD's own success_metrics fixture expectations) bounds how long the scheduled step waits before finalizing an outcome for a row. If the window elapses and the platform lookup could not be completed (network/auth error, not a 404/deleted result), the row is left 'unknown' for the next run rather than coerced to any terminal outcome -- distinct from FR-1's 'unmeasurable' (permanently unobservable) case. A literal dry-run-* sentinel or null external_post_id is rejected immediately as unmeasurable (FR-1) BEFORE the fixed-window logic ever runs -- it is not a "transient failure inside the window" case.
acceptance_criteria: A transient lookup failure inside the window leaves the row 'unknown', re-attempted on the next scheduled run
A row past the window with a confirmed-absent post is classified 'reverted', never left 'unknown' forever

system_architecture.summary: A new read-only observer module joins the publish ledger to campaign_content to recover real post ids, looks posts up via two new adapter methods, and feeds the existing (currently unreachable) mode-aware graduation path through a scheduled job -- never through publish() itself. recordPublishOutcome/evaluateGraduation are modified (not reused as-is) to add the execution_mode scoping validation found missing. A durable dispatch-key fix in publisher/index.js is the load-bearing prerequisite the observer join depends on -- build and test it first.

implementation_approach.summary: Build the join+classify core first against a fixture, then the two adapter lookups, then wire the scheduled job, then the additive migration, verifying idempotency and mode isolation before touching evaluateGraduation's real call path.
steps: FIRST: fix publisher/index.js to use authCheck.correlationId for the campaign_content dedup/upsert key, and prove it with a real two-attempt approval-gated integration test (FR-1, TS-1) -- nothing downstream can be verified against reality until this lands
Implement observeOutcome's ledger-to-campaign_content join and unmeasurable/unknown classification against a fixture (FR-1, TS-1, TS-4)
Add Bluesky getPostRecord and X getTweet read-only lookups (FR-2, FR-3)
Wire observeOutcome's live-post-state branch through the two new adapter lookups
Build scripts/cron/publish-outcome-observer.mjs + workflow + armed-registration + stamp-last-fired, calling recordPublishOutcome per row (FR-4, TS-2)
Write and apply the additive outcome-enum migration (FR-6)
Run evaluateGraduation from a real recorded live outcome and confirm graduation reachability
Add an execution_mode predicate to recordPublishOutcome's update and a mode filter to evaluateGraduation's candidate SELECT (FR-5)
Prove the full pipeline end-to-end against a self-created mock-mode fixture only; do not attempt any real AltifyAI (or other real venture) post this increment (FR-8)
Confirm the dependency SD's owed inline recordPublishOutcome call is not built anywhere (TR-5)
Widen recordPublishOutcome's JS allowlist and evaluateGraduation's streak-window query together with the SQL migration (FR-6, TS-9, TS-10)
Add rows_selected/rows_joined/rows_unmeasurable counters to the scheduled step's summary (FR-4, TS-11)
Add options.fetchImpl DI seam to both adapter constructors; rewrite adapter tests against mocked HTTP status, never live APIs (TR-7)
